subject: Proof of Controlled Replication and Deletion for Customer VPC Stores - Q&A
body:
--- Message 1 (2026-09-21T09:15:00-07:00) ---
From: Elena Ramirez <elena.ramirez@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novahealth.com
Subject: Questions on replication and certified deletion for our VPC store

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Nova Health is very interested but we need to clarify a few technical guarantees for our legal and security teams before we can proceed. Two core items: 

1) Replication topology: can you confirm whether data stored in our customer-controlled VPC bucket is ever replicated outside the customer-designated region? We need to list exactly which processes (backups, snapshots, failover) may create copies and where those copies reside.

2) Certified deletion: when Nova requests a tenant-level erase, what evidence can Redwood provide that proves the data and derived artifacts were removed from all layers (hot caches, KV cache, snapshots, object storage, backups)? Our audit requires a signed attestation and a chain-of-custody timeline.

Could you point us to a sample attestation and rough timelines for each step? Attachments: I will share our internal checklist if useful.

Best,
Elena
Head of Security Operations
Nova Health

--- Message 2 (2026-09-21T10:03:00-07:00) ---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena.ramirez@novahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Questions on replication and certified deletion for our VPC store

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:
- Replication: By default, customer VPC object stores are not geo-replicated automatically by Redwood. Any cross-region replication is only performed if explicitly configured by the customer or as part of an opt-in DR program and is documented in the deployment config.
- Deletion proof: We provide an erase-audit artifact (signed) listing steps taken: cache invalidation, KV tombstoning, snapshot tombstone, object-store purge, and backup purge scheduling.

Ill loop in Marissa and Ben to provide the procedural details and an example attestation document. Timeline: typical complete evidence package is 48–72 hours for non-emergency erases (can be expedited).

Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 (2026-09-21T13:22:00-07:00) ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena.ramirez@novahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Questions on replication and certified deletion for our VPC store

Hi Elena — following up with an operational breakdown. Ive attached a high-level replication architecture diagram and an erase-audit checklist (see attachments). Below is a condensed Q&A that maps to your two asks.

Replication topology (what we do / do not do)
- Customer VPC stores: created in the region you select; Redwood does not perform background geo-replication across regions unless the customer has explicitly enabled a cross-region replication rule in the VPC config or enrolled in our DR replication add-on.
- Snapshots/backups: periodic snapshots are taken per the deployments configured snapshot window. Snapshots are stored in the same region by default. For customers who choose cross-region backup for regulatory reasons, we record the destinations in the deployment manifest and require additional customer authorization.
- Failover scenarios: in immediate failover (region outage), we may temporarily instantiate a read-only replica in a permitted DR region only if you have authorized this in the manifest. Any such instantiation is always audited and short-lived; we provide a timeline and proof of instantiation to the customer.

Deletion & evidence (stepwise)
1) Invalidate active caches: streaming/serving KV caches are invalidated immediately; eviction events are logged with timestamps and node ids.
2) Mark logical tombstone: tenant ID marked in control plane as deleted (this prevents new reads and triggers downstream purge workflows).
3) Object store purge: we issue delete operations against object buckets; delete confirmations and object-level delete markers are recorded.
4) Snapshot/backup scrub: scheduled snapshot retention jobs mark snapshots for purge and update an audit ledger; for encrypted backups we rotate and destroy keys where applicable.
5) Final verification & attestation: ops compiles a signed erase-audit document (includes sha256s of deleted manifests where feasible), timeline with operator IDs, and system logs.

Typical SLAs
- Cache invalidation: immediate (within minutes)
- Object store deletion confirmation: within 24 hours (depends on storage provider semantics)
- Snapshot/backup purge completion: 24–72 hours (varies if cross-region purge is required)
- Full erase attestation delivered: 48–72 hours

Attachments: replication-architecture-diagram.pdf, erase-audit-checklist.xlsx

Let me know if you need a template attestation in legal-friendly language; Ben can propose contract wording.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Cc: security@novahealth.com
Subject: Re: Questions on replication and certified deletion for our VPC store

Thanks Marissa — this helps a lot. A couple follow-ups where we need specificity for our compliance review: 

- Evidence format: wed prefer an attestation PDF with an operator signature + a machine-signed ledger extract (or similar) that shows delete ops and timestamps. Is that possible?
- Proof of non-replication: can Redwood provide a deployment manifest excerpt on request that confirms no cross-region replication rules were present at time of deletion?

Also, for contract exhibits — we will need a clause that says Redwood will not replicate customer VPC buckets outside the designated region unless authorized in writing and that any emergency DR action requires 24-hour notice to Nova Security (unless Nova explicitly opts into automated DR). Can you propose language?

Regards,
Elena

--- Message 5 (2026-09-23T17:02:00-07:00) ---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramirez <elena.ramirez@novahealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Subject: Re: Questions on replication and certified deletion for our VPC store

Elena — appreciate the specificity. Below is draft contract language (we can iterate) and a confirmation on the evidence bundle.

Draft exhibit wording (suggested):
"Redwood Inference will not perform cross-region replication of customer-controlled VPC object stores except where the customer has explicitly configured a replication rule or has executed Redwood's documented Disaster Recovery (DR) enrollment process. Any temporary instantiation of resources in alternate regions for the purposes of failover will only occur with prior written authorization, except in the event of an active, declared regional outage. In the event of such an outage, Redwood will notify the customers security contact within 24 hours of instantiation, and will provide an automatic teardown of temporary replicas once the primary region is restored, together with a signed instantiation log and timeline."

Evidence bundle: we can provide a PDF attestation signed by the on-duty operations lead plus a machine-signed ledger extract (immutable log entries) that includes delete operation hashes, timestamps, and the object keys/manifest references where feasible. For manifests that include sensitive identifiers, we can provide redacted copies and a hash to prove the record existed.

Next steps
- I will upload the sample attestation and the manifest excerpt template to the Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLink) and share the RDW-9342 support ticket to track the formal attestation production.
- If youre comfortable, Jordan can schedule a 30-minute legal/ops sync to finalize exhibit language.

Ben Carter
Head of Technical Partnerships, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: replication-architecture-diagram.pdf, erase-audit-checklist.xlsx]
